carmen: quick thread - after the canary deploy (deploy/2026-03-17) we see ~10% higher p99 token latency on some workloads, looks correlated with KV cache miss rate spike. :frowning:
ashwin: saw that in perf dashboard, KV hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 78% on longctx workloads.
kevin: which change touched keys? I pushed the canonicalization patch yesterday that normalizes whitespace in prompts.
carmen: yep that's the one. It switched from raw prompt fingerprint to normalized sha1(prefix + tenant) -> now we're using tenant first. suspect collision in prefix ordering.
lucy: profiler (perf-bot run): https://perf.internal/runs/2026/173880 - kv_p99_latency jump at 00:12:43
perf-bot: perf job finished: https://perf.internal/jobs/kv-reuse-173880 - summary attached
ashwin: I pulled the flamegraph: majority of time is in kv.get + deserialization; but miss rate increased so more page reads. attached snippet:
```
kv:misses=12456 hits=44720 hit_ratio=0.782
memory:kv_alloc=12.3GB rss=22.1GB
evictions:recent=8k pages_paged=3.2k
```
kevin: hmm, changing key ordering could change sharding distribution -> fragmentation. Also might have affected prefix coalescing logic in cache layer.
carmen: agree. longctx sessions saw memory growth over multiple requests, probably because cache entries not matching across requests (prefix mismatch) so we keep allocating new entries instead of reusing.
lucy: repro: run local harness with longctx sim: `./dev/run_harness --scenario longctx --repeat 1000` shows steady kv_alloc increase until OOM.
ashwin: short term fix: revert canonicalization or add stable canonical key function. proposal:
```
stable_key = sha1(tenant + '\n' + normalize_whitespace(prefix))
```
kevin: also add an optional session_sticky flag so same session uses session-scoped salt to increase reuse.
carmen: action items: 1) kevin revert canonicalization in canary (owner: kevin) 2) ashwin run a sharding sim to see branch distribution (owner: ashwin) 3) lucy add deterministic repro and memory trace (owner: lucy). I'll open a rollback PR if we don't have a safe fix in 2h. :hourglass: 
kevin: ack. starting rollback now.
lucy: adding perf counters to kv: prefixed_hits, canonical_mismatch_counter, page_reads.
perf-bot: trace: https://traces.internal/trace/173880/kv_regression
ashwin: FYI this also impacted batching heuristics slightly (more small batches), because more misses -> longer backend work.
carmen: thanks all, ping me if you can't reproduce. We'll close out once sharding sim confirms fragmentation cause. :thumbsup:
